evidence: This is stated as a finding and shown in Figure 2F.

claim: No significant differences in either viremia or fraction of PLWH with undetectable ART were observed in either wave between timepoints which were SARS-CoV-2 positive and those that were negative.
source: We observed no significant differences in either viremia or fraction of PLWH with undetectable ART in either wave between timepoints which were SARS-CoV-2 positive and those that were negative (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated as a finding and shown in a figure supplement.

claim: The increase in the CD4 was not due to better linkage to care after the hospital visit but rather due to SARS-CoV-2 clearance.
source: This indicates that the increase in the CD4 was not due to better linkage to care after the hospital visit but rather due to SARS-CoV-2 clearance.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the data.

claim: A significant decrease in the fraction of CXCR3 expressing CD8 T cells in the blood compartment was observed in PLWH relative to HIV-negative participants during active SARS-CoV-2 infection in wave 1.
source: In CD8 T cells, we observed a significant decrease in the fraction of CXCR3 expressing cells in the blood compartment in PLWH relative to HIV-negative participants (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated as a finding and shown in Figure 4A.

claim: An increase in the fraction of PD-1+HLA-DR+ CD8 T cells was observed in PLWH relative to HIV-negative participants during active SARS-CoV-2 infection in wave 1.
source: We also observed an increase in the fraction of PD-1+HLA-DR+ cells (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated as a finding and shown in Figure 4B.

claim: There was an increase in PD-1+HLA-DR+ CD4 T cells in PLWH relative to HIV-negative participants during active SARS-CoV-2 infection in wave 1.
source: Similarly to CD8 T cells, there was an increase in PD-1+HLA-DR+ CD4 T cells in PLWH (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is stated as a finding and shown in Figure 4D.

claim: There was no difference between PLWH and HIV-negative participants in any cell/marker combination after SARS-CoV-2 clearance.
source: There was no difference between PLWH and HIV-negative participants in any cell/marker combination after SARS-CoV-2 clearance.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study data.

claim: COVID-19 disease severity was higher in PLWH in the cohort.
source: We observed that in our cohort, COVID-19 disease severity was higher in PLWH, consistent with some of the larger epidemiological studies (Western Cape Department of Health in collaboration with the National Institute for Communicable Diseases, South Africa et al., 2021; Geretti et al., 2021; Bhaskaran et al., 2021; Tesoriero et al., 2021; Braunstein et al., 2021; Jassat et al., 2021a)
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study with citations to supporting literature.

claim: Differences in disease severity were detected in the frequency of participants requiring supplemental oxygen and not in mortality.
source: although in this study differences were detected in the frequency of participants requiring supplemental oxygen and not in mortality.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study data.

claim: The odds ratio for requiring supplemental oxygen in the second wave for PLWH was 4.0 relative to HIV negative participants.
source: The odds ratio for requiring supplemental oxygen in the second wave for PLWH was 4.0 relative to HIV negative participants.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study data.

claim: The 95% confidence intervals for the odds ratio of requiring supplemental oxygen in wave 2 for PLWH were wide at 1.6–10.4.
source: The 95% confidence intervals were wide at 1.6–10.4, reflecting the relatively small number of participants.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study data.

claim: The substantial recovery of CD4 T cell counts in PLWH after SARS-CoV-2 clearance in wave 2 may be consistent with the Beta variant having more impact on the CD4 count relative to the ancestral SARS-CoV-2 strain infections in the first wave.
source: Furthermore, the substantial recovery of CD4 T cell counts in PLWH after SARS-CoV-2 clearance in wave 2 may be consistent with the Beta variant having more impact on the CD4 count relative to the ancestral SARS-CoV-2 strain infections in the first wave.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the findings.

claim: The role of the Beta variant is supported by data showing extensive evolution, increasing the ability of Beta to escape the interferon response and result in more efficient viral cell-to-cell transmission.
source: The role of the Beta variant is supported by data showing extensive evolution, increasing the ability of Beta to escape the interferon response and result in more efficient viral cell-to-cell transmission (Guo et al., 2021; Thorne et al., 2021; Rajah et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated with citations to support the claim.

claim: Beta variant hospitalizations led to more deaths in South Africa.
source: Beta variant hospitalizations also led to more deaths in South Africa (Jassat et al., 2021b).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to support the claim.

claim: The increase in PD-1+HLA-DR+ T cells indicates T cell activation which associates with worse COVID-19 outcomes.
source: The increase in PD-1+HLA-DR+ T cells indicates T cell activation (Sauce et al., 2007; Vollbrecht et al., 2010) which associates with worse COVID-19 outcomes (Chen et al., 2020b).
evidence: This is stated with citations to support the claim.

claim: CXCR3 plays a key role in T cell homing to sites of inflammation.
source: CXCR3 plays a key role in T cell homing to sites of inflammation and is activated by interferon-inducible ligands CXCL9, CXCL11, and CXCL10 (IP-10) (Groom and Luster, 2011; Rodda et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated with citations to support the claim.
